IN THE COURT OF APPEALS OF THE STATE OF OREGON

and
Rochelle Danielle Deidre Petty,
Respondent-Respondent.
Washington County Circuit Court No. 17DR19361
Court of Appeals No. A185721
ORDER DENYING ATTORNEY FEES; AWARDING COSTS
Before Egan, Presiding Judge, and Joyce, Judge.
Father has prevailed in this appeal of the trial court’s decision to grant mother
temporary custody and parenting time of the parties’ children under an immediate-danger
order. See ORS 107.139. Now, father seeks an award of attorney fees in the
amount of $9,450 and costs in the amount of $947.75. Mother opposes the request for
attorney fees. Neither side requests findings under ORAP 13.10(7).
As for costs, which are allowed, father requests $391 for the filing fee and
$556.75 for the transcript fee. Both costs are recoverable under ORS 20.310, and they
are awarded to father.
As for attorney fees, father asserts that awarding him fees for work performed in
connection with this appeal “is proper under ORS 107.135(8), 107.434(2)(d), and
20.075.” However, as mother points out, none of the rules or statutes cited by father in
the petition authorize the court to award appellate attorney fees to father. Even
assuming there existed an authority that did authorize an award of fees to father, the
court would deny father’s request based on the relevant ORS 20.075 factors.
In sum, father is awarded costs in the amount of $947.75; father’s petition for
attorney fees is denied.
James C. Egan
Presiding Judge
5/28/2026

The parties jointly move under ORAP 10.35 to reverse the parts of the trial

IN THE COURT OF APPEALS OF THE STATE OF OREGON
CRAFT RENOVATIONS INC., an Oregon corporation,
Plaintiff-Appellant,
v.
SHANA HARRIS, an individual,
Defendant,
and
MICHAEL B. HARRIS, an individual, and LILY TSEN, an individual,
Defendants-Respondents.
_____________________________________________________________________
SHANA HARRIS, an individual,
Plaintiff,
v.
CRAFT RENOVATIONS INC., an Oregon corporation, and JEFF L'ALLIER,
Defendants.
Washington County Circuit Court No. 22CV09639
Court of Appeals No. A180016
ORDER DENYING ATTORNEY FEES AND AWARDING COSTS
Before Egan, Presiding Judge, and Joyce, Judge.
In this anti-SLAPP case, respondents petition for $25,540 in attorney fees under
ORS 31.152(3) and for $597 in costs. Appellant (Craft Renovations) objects to an
award of fees. Neither side requests findings pursuant to ORAP 13.10(7). For the
reasons explained below, the court denies attorney fees and award $491 in costs.
As an initial matter, the court strikes the pro se filings by Shana Harris and
Michael Harris. As the court has already made clear in prior orders, Shana Harris is not
a party to this appeal, nor is she an attorney. Respondent Michael Harris is represented
by counsel on appeal. See ORS 9.320 (“Where a party appears by attorney, the written
proceedings must be through attorney.).
As for costs, which are allowed per the court’s opinion, the court concludes that
of the costs requested by respondents, the court only has authority to award the $391
ORDER DENYING ATTORNEY FEES AND AWARDING COSTS
Appellate Court Administrator, Appellate Court Records Section
1163 State Street, Salem, Oregon 97301-2563
Page 2 of 2
first appearance fee and the $100 prevailing party fee. See ORS 20.310. Therefore,
the court awards $491 in costs to respondents.
As for attorney fees, respondents rely on ORS 31.152(3). Under that statute, a
court is required to award reasonable attorney fees to “[a] defendant who prevails on a
special motion to strike.” ORS 31.152(3). On the other hand, the court is required to
award reasonable attorney fees “to a plaintiff who prevails on a special motion to strike”
only if the court finds that the special motion to strike “is frivolous or is solely intended to
cause unnecessary delay.” Id.
Here, the court agrees with Craft Renovations that respondents, as the side that
brought the slander-of-title claim that was the subject of the special motion to strike, are
properly considered “plaintiff[s]” for the purpose of ORS 31.152(3). Craft Renovations
Inc. v. Harris, 340 Or App 33, 36 n 2, 570 P3d 629 (2025) (Explaining that the reference
in ORS 31.150 “to the parties by their role as plaintiff and defendant are reversed in the
current matter, as the claim at issue was a counterclaim filed by the defendants against
the plaintiff.”). Accordingly, in order for respondents to be entitled to attorney fees, the
court must find that Craft Renovations’ motion to strike was either “frivolous” or “solely
intended to cause unnecessary delay.” See ORS 31.152(3). Having considered the
parties’ arguments and the issues raised on appeal, the court disagrees with
respondents that Craft Renovations’ motion to strike (or appeal in support of the motion
to strike) was “frivolous.”
Respondents’ petition for attorney fees is denied. Respondents are awarded
costs in the amount of $491.
James C. Egan
Presiding Judge
2/25/2026

Defendant-Respondent.
Umatilla County Circuit Court No. 22CV07157
Court of Appeals No. A186198
ORDER OF SUMMARY AFFIRMANCE
Before Egan, Presiding Judge, and Joyce, Judge.
Respondent (the superintendent) moves pursuant to ORS 138.660 for summary
affirmance on the ground that the appeal does not present a substantial question of law.
Petitioner opposes the motion.
The court determines that, for the reasons articulated in the superintendent’s
motion, petitioner’s brief does not present a substantial question of law regarding
whether the post-conviction court erred in denying post-conviction relief. Specifically,
petitioner has failed to raise a substantial question of law regarding, at the least, the
assertion of prejudice as a result of trial counsel’s alleged defective performance
because the post-conviction court’s adverse credibility determination is supported by
evidence in the record. Hale v. Belleque, 255 Or App 653, 660, 298 P3d 596, adh'd to
on recons, 258 Or App 587, rev den, 354 Or 597 (2013) (this court is “bound by the
post-conviction court’s findings of fact, if they are supported by any evidence in the
record”); see Moen v. Peterson, 312 Or 503, 513, 824 P2d 404 (1991). Therefore, the
motion is granted.
Affirmed.
James C. Egan
Presiding Judge
6/15/2026

ORDER ALLOWING COSTS AND AWARDING CONDITIONAL ATTORNEY FEES

Washington County Circuit Court No. 22DR12736
Court of Appeals No. A184834
ORDER ALLOWING COSTS AND AWARDING CONDITIONAL ATTORNEY FEES
Before Egan, Presiding Judge, and Joyce, Judge.
In this domestic relations case, father appealed from a supplemental judgment
awarding attorney fees, which this court vacated and remanded. Accordingly, father, as
the prevailing party, seeks costs in the amount of $1,846, as well as $9,975 in attorney
fees pursuant to ORS 107.135(8). Mother argues that, because the outcome may not
change on remand, an award of fees should await the trial court's decision. See ORAP
13.10(3) (appellate court may condition award of attorney fees on the ultimate outcome
of the case on remand). Neither party requests findings under ORS 13.10(7).
As for costs, father requests $391 for the filing fee and $1,455 for the transcript.
Both costs are recoverable under ORS 20.310 and are uncontested. Therefore, father
is awarded costs in the amount of $1,846.
As for attorney fees, the court awards father the total amount of fees he requests,
conditioned under ORAP 13.10(3) on him ultimately prevailing on remand. With respect
to entitlement to recover appellate fees, ORS 20.075(1) governs our exercise of
discretion to award fees, together with equitable considerations. See, e.g., Githens and
Githens, 230 Or App 568, 593, 216 P3d 904, rev den, 347 Or 42 (2009). Having
considered the parties' arguments and the ORS 20.075(1) factors, the court determines
that it is appropriate to exercise discretion, pursuant to ORS 107.135(8), to award
reasonable attorney fees to father. Further, mother does not challenge the amount of
fees father requests as unreasonable. In any event, having considered the ORS
ORDER ALLOWING COSTS AND AWARDING CONDITIONAL ATTORNEY FEES

20.075(1) and (2) factors, we determine that it is reasonable to award father the $9,975
in fees requested. Lastly, under the totality of the circumstances, we determine that it is
appropriate to exercise discretion under ORAP 13.10(3) to condition the award of fees
on father prevailing on remand.
In sum, father is awarded costs in the amount of $1,846 and is conditionally
awarded attorney fees in the amount of $9,975.

Petitioner, in an unopposed motion, moves the court to vacate the board’s final
order setting petitioner’s sex offender notification level and remand the case.1 Petitioner
represents that the board does not object to the motion. The case, which was held in
abeyance, is reactivated, and the motion is granted.
The court agrees with the parties that the proper disposition of this case is to

notification level, pursuant to Harless v. Board of Parole, 348 Or App 289, ___ P3d ___

Harless, because the appropriate outcome under Harless is vacating and remanding the

disposition is appropriate in this case.

IN THE COURT OF APPEALS OF THE STATE OF OREGON
In the Matter of the Compensation of Sandra Ferrusca-Corona, Claimant.
The Sherwin Williams Company and Gallagher Bassett Services Inc.,
Petitioners,
v.
Sandra Ferrusca-Corona,
Respondent.
Workers' Compensation Board No. 2201943
Court of Appeals No. A185981
ORDER AWARDING ATTORNEY FEES AND COSTS
Before Egan, Presiding Judge, and Joyce, Judge.
In this worker’s compensation case, The Sherwin Williams Company (employer)
sought judicial review of the Workers' Compensation Board’s order. Per employer’s
motion to dismiss, the court entered an order of dismissal on October 28, 2025. The
order of dismissal designated claimant as the prevailing party and the court later
amended the order so as to allow costs payable by employer.
Having prevailed on judicial review, claimant petitions for attorney fees in the
amount of $11,350, pursuant to ORS 656.386(1)(a), as well as costs in the amount of
$100. Employer opposes the amount of fees claimant request. Neither party requests
findings. See ORAP 13.10(7).
As for costs, as noted above, they are allowed. Claimant requests $100 for what
appears to be the prevailing party fee. See ORS 20.190(1)(a) (setting the prevailing
party fee in the Court of Appeals at $100). That cost is recoverable under ORS 20.310,
and it is awarded.
As for fees, the parties agree that ORS 656.386(1)(a) entitles claimant to an
award of reasonable attorney fees in this case. That statute provides, in relevant part:
“In all cases involving denied claims where a claimant finally prevails against the denial
in an appeal to the Court of Appeals or petition for review to the Supreme Court, the
court shall allow a reasonable attorney fee to the claimant’s attorney.” ORS
656.386(1)(a). The court agrees with the parties that the statute applies so as to entitle
claimant to reasonable fees.
ORDER AWARDING ATTORNEY FEES AND COSTS
Appellate Court Administrator, Appellate Court Records Section
1163 State Street, Salem, Oregon 97301-2563
Page 2 of 2
The factors under ORS 20.075 guide the court’s determination of the amount of
attorney fees to award. Having considered those factors, as well as the parties’
arguments, the court is persuaded that the $11,350 in fees requested by claimant in the
fee petition is a reasonable amount. To the extent that claimant requests an additional
amount of fees for work in replying to employer’s objection, the court determines that it
is appropriate to deny that request, especially given the fact that, as claimant
acknowledges, the reply provides the statement of tasks performed that should have
been included in the initial fee petition. See ORAP 13.10(5)(a).
In sum, the court awards claimant $11,350 in attorney fees and $100 in costs.
James C. Egan
Presiding Judge
